Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating Mr. Julian Vance, a 35-year-old software analyst referred for further specialized assessment.

Mr. Vance attended my clinic for a baseline visual check. He is generally healthy, takes no routine medications, and reports no family history of visual impairment. On functional inquiry, he actively denies any difficulties with night vision or delayed dark adaptation.

On examination, his uncorrected visual acuity was excellent at 20/20 in each eye. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy of the anterior segments and applanation tonometry were entirely within normal limits. Dilated funduscopy revealed healthy, well-perfused optic nerve heads with sharp margins and no disc pallor. Retinal arteriolar and venular calibers were well preserved, showing no vascular attenuation. Thorough peripheral retinal inspection demonstrated no bone-spicule pigment deposits and an absence of scalloped chorioretinal atrophy.

However, on baseline electrodiagnostic evaluation, his full-field electroretinogram proved clearly abnormal, displaying altered scotopic and photopic wave amplitudes and atypical timing across both eyes.

Given these unexpected electrophysiological perturbations in the context of an otherwise unremarkable structural exam, I would be very grateful for your formal evaluation and guidance regarding further investigation or surveillance.

Sincerely,
Dr. Laura Bennett
